classification.difficultyReason: Use inverse tangent on a journey diagram and express the resulting clockwise angle from north as a three-digit true bearing.

content.prompt: Anne travelled 7 km due north from Ben’s house and then 12 km due east to Carol’s house. What is the true bearing from Ben’s house to Carol’s house? Answer to the nearest degree.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 diagram below the prompt on the left
spec.description: Right triangle with a 7 km northward leg, a 12 km eastward leg, a right angle at the northwest vertex, endpoint dots and a four-direction compass at Ben’s house. Ordinary source colours are replaced by black.
spec.mathematics: Ben’s house is at (0,0), the turning point at (0,7), and Carol’s house at (12,7). The unknown acute angle theta runs clockwise from north to the diagonal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the unknown theta and supplied lengths are visible; the numerical bearing is answer-only.

answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\dfrac{12}{7}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{12}{7}\right)\\\theta&\approx60^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The angle is measured clockwise from north, so the true bearing is $060^{\circ}$.
